inputs: the user's menu numbers and any formula
3a.evidence: the dry-run JSON; the written config after confirmation
3a.rung_why: The menus are code and T9 is a human confirmation (R1 plus R3), but whether any decisions remain (R-required), how a scrnaseq chemistry is chosen (R-protocol), which factor the contrast compares (R-factor) and what counts as the confirmation (R-confirm) have no rule, how words become a formula has a written rule nothing checks (R-formula), and on a closed project the guard refuses contrasts and apply (G-closed).

silent.decision: How a scrnaseq user's library chemistry gets into the config
silent.goes_wrong: configure.py makes chemistry scrnaseq's decision and has a protocols menu, but step 3a and T8 name only the genome, contrast and peak menus, and 3a's apply line carries no --protocol, so for scrnaseq it exits 3 (configure.py:411-414). The model either adds --protocol itself, translating the user's words into one of the listed chemistries, or stalls; a wrong but listed chemistry runs to completion and parses barcodes with the wrong layout
silent.why_rank: A plausible wrong matrix and no error; the scrnaseq sub-stage's human check tells every user to compare cell counts with the number loaded and names wrong chemistry as a cause
silent.fix: Step 3a runs `configure.py protocols --aligner <a>` for protocol assays, T8 renders it, T9 confirms it

silent.decision: Turning the user's words about the model ('account for batch') into a DE formula
silent.goes_wrong: Scope allows a formula 'the user gave you', and users give words, not formula syntax; the model writes the formula and apply checks only that each term names a column of the design table, so a wrong covariate or interaction becomes the tested model
silent.why_rank: A wrong model changes every p-value; T9 asks the user to confirm the formula, a real check only for a user who reads formula syntax
silent.fix: Formula choices built from the design table's own columns, as the contrasts are, confirmed in T9

silent.decision: Whether the config still has decisions to make
silent.goes_wrong: 3a is skipped when 'no <REQUIRED> markers are left', judged by the model reading YAML; every seeded config carries the word in its header comment and spatialvi has no decisions registered, so a literal reading re-asks a finished config or runs apply for spatialvi, which exits 3 with no branch
silent.why_rank: A stall or a needless question, not a wrong result
silent.fix: Code reports the pending decisions (the wrappers' config_unfilled check already computes them)

silent.decision: Which design factor the contrast compares
silent.goes_wrong: contrasts and apply default to --factor condition (configure.py:501, 517), which no contract mentions; when the design carries another factor the user cares about, the model decides which one the menu is built from. silent.decision: When to refresh a submitted job's STATUS, and who does it
silent.goes_wrong: STATUS moves from SUBMITTED to VALIDATING when executorlib.py status (or collect's own gate) asks the scheduler, but the router stops on SUBMITTED or RUNNING and sends the user to squeue, and every sub-stage's step 2 stops too; the sub-stage's own status step is behind both, so it runs only if the model decides to poll on its own or the user runs a status command a template showed them. A finished job can look 'still running' indefinitely, or the model polls in a loop the scope forbids
silent.why_rank: A stall the user has to sort out, and a visible one; but every assay passes through it
silent.fix: The router calls status once before routing a SUBMITTED or RUNNING sub-stage
